name: Bansi Vihar
why_it_matters: A pure-veg South Indian room on Frazer Road that opened in 1994 and became the default family lunch spot for travellers walking out of Patna Junction. Ranked top-10 on Patna's TripAdvisor list for over a decade.
insider_tip: Avoid weekend lunch (1-3pm) — the queue outside the lift can run twenty minutes. The filter coffee is genuinely brewed, not pre-mixed; ask for it after the meal.
signature_address: Frazer Road, near Bank of India, Frazer Road Area, Patna 800001

name: Pind - The Revolving Restaurant
why_it_matters: Patna's only revolving restaurant, on the 18th floor of Biscomaun Tower opposite Gandhi Maidan. The full rotation gives a 360-degree view of the Ganga, Golghar and the maidan; food is supporting cast for the view.
insider_tip: Book a window table for a sunset slot (around 6pm in winter) — the Golghar sits in line with the river behind it. The menu skews North Indian-Chinese; stick to biryani and tikka rather than the continental side.
signature_address: 16th-18th floors, Biscomaun Bhawan, Gandhi Maidan Road, Patna 800001

name: DK Litti
why_it_matters: Multi-outlet litti takeaway run for around 16 years across Hariniwas Complex, Mithapur and Kankarbagh. Coal-cooked litti and three chokhas served in foil — closest you get to a Frazer Road street version with a printed bill.
insider_tip: Takeaway-first; the seating is minimal. Skip the 'fried litti' on the menu — it's the roasted version that holds up over the ride home.
signature_address: Hariniwas Complex, Bailey Road / Fraser Road Area, Patna 800001

name: Maner Sweets
why_it_matters: Brings the syrupy layered khaja from Silao village (40 km out) into Patna proper. The maner laddoo got national-stage attention after PM Modi referenced it in a Bihar election speech, but the khaja is the older draw.
insider_tip: Khaja loses crunch within 24 hours; buy what you'll eat that night. The shop tins khaja for travel but it goes chewy by day three — the laddoo version travels better.

name: Biryani Mahal
why_it_matters: A Frazer Road biryani counter that has built its reputation on the meat-to-rice ratio rather than ambiance — small dining room, takeaway-heavy, listed on every Patna biryani round-up.
insider_tip: Order the mutton biryani over chicken — the slow-cooked shanks are what regulars come for. Friday dinner sells out by 10pm.

name: Vaishali Cafe
why_it_matters: The 24-hour coffee shop at Hotel Maurya — Bihar's first luxury hotel, opened 1978 next to Gandhi Maidan. The breakfast buffet is where Patna does its Saturday family meal; the rest of the day it works as a calm meeting room with consistent food.
insider_tip: The buffet runs 7-10am and includes a Bihari section (litti, chokha, sattu paratha) most weekday mornings — a faster way to sample the regional spread than chasing individual stalls.
signature_address: Hotel Maurya, South Gandhi Maidan, Patna 800001
